newsitem.title: USA: N.J. Gov. Whitman outlines auto reform plan.
newsitem.headline: N.J. Gov. Whitman outlines auto reform plan.

text.p: Gov. Christine Whitman proposed Tuesday revising New Jersey's auto insurance law to offer consumers four options, two of which should help keep premiums down.

New Jersey has the nation's highest average premium at $964. Whitman proposed two low-cost options. In the first a driver surrenders his right to sue. In the second, a driver agrees to accept a pre-determined schedule of compensation for injuries.
The third option allows drivers to sue for pain and suffering once a verbal threshold is met, and the final, most costly option would allow recovery by lawsuit for all losses.

The governor estimated the most restrictive option would reduce premiums by 25 percent. She also proposed to enhance initiatives against fraud, which she estimated adds $150 to the average annual premium.

In an address otherwise lacking major new proposals in the beginning of the year she will campaign for her re-election, whitman pledged to sign a new bill giving small, so-called "sub- chapter S" corporations a tax break. She noted that these are usually small businesses more akin to the partnerships that their taxes would be modeled on.
The governor estimated that it would cost the treasury $13 million in lost revenue.

She claimed success for the 30-percent cut in income taxes for most New Jerseyans enacted in the first three years of her first term, saying it turned around a recession-wracked economy. She was silent about a proposal to float $3.4 billion in bonds to fully fund the state's pension system, but the Democratic opposition criticized it as more budget balancing with new debt.
Whitman is scheduled to deliver a budget message Jan 29.
